patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Microsoft Teams share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Dialpad only if your buying job matches “AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard fr” rather than Microsoft Teams's shape. Choose Microsoft Teams only if your buying job matches “M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on ” rather than Dialpad's shape. Workflow advantage: Dialpad leans business-phone, sales-calling; Microsoft Teams leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Microsoft Teams share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Dialpad is AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard from $15/user/month annual; Sell and Support are sep; Microsoft Teams is M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on — free Teams tier exists; Phone Standard ~$10/user.
- Workflow coverage skew: Dialpad-leaning business-phone, sales-calling vs Microsoft Teams-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Dialpad — Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Microsoft Teams — Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job.

Limitations — Dialpad: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Connect Pro has a 3-user minimum; Enterprise requires 100 users; Microsoft Teams: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job; Teams Phone requires an eligible Teams/M365 licence plus PSTN (PAYG or Calling Plan).

Poor-fit cases: Dialpad is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price · Microsoft Teams is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job · Avoid Dialpad if you actually need Microsoft Teams's motion (M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telepho)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
